messages:
samir: Heads up — canary in eu-west just showed a sustained p95 regression (~220ms -> 420ms) after the 2.7.0 rollout. Deploy-bot flagged it as a potential rollback.
deploy-bot: deploybot:signal: latency_p95 > threshold for 3m in eu-west. Suggested action: \n - recommendation: STAGGERED_REWIND (10% -> 30% -> 100%)\n - auto_revert: OFF (requires operator confirm)\n - reason: kernel selector change + new kv-cache ttl behavior
lia: @samir can you paste the smoke logs? is it errors or just higher tail?
samir: errors are low (5xx still normal) — it's latency tail, likely KV miss pattern after the new cache TTL tweak. attaching a small snippet:
```
2026-03-23T10:12:05Z INFO request_id=abc123 p95=438ms route=/gen model=gptx-v2 kernel=fastkv
2026-03-23T10:12:06Z INFO request_id=def456 p95=426ms route=/chat model=gptx-v2 kernel=fastkv
```
maya: agree with manual intervention. We should avoid full immediate revert; do staggered rewind to the previous kernel flag and verify metrics after each step. ops-oncall you good to run the rewind? we need comms to customers if we escalate.
ops-oncall: can do. propose plan: \n 1) pin eu-west traffic back to kernel=v1.9 (10% slice)\n 2) wait 5m, check p95 and error rate\n 3) escalate to 30% then 100% if stable.\nI will notify support for customer watchlist.
julian: add automated smoke eval after each slice: run eval set "canary_smoke_v2" and fail if regressions on top-k or latency. If eval fails, stop and hold for triage.
samir: sounds good. also add release notes line about kernel flag fallback and create a small blurb for the status page.
lia: draft for incident cadence: \n- ACTION: ops-oncall executes staggered rewind\n- COMMS: samir + maya will draft status update, support will post in #incidents if customers report\n- POST: if rewind completes, we create a postmortem explaining why kernel selector triggered regressions and a rollback checklist

maya: +1. we should also temporarily disable autoscale-burst to keep signal clean.
ops-oncall: executing step 1 now: `infractl rewind --region eu-west --slice 10 --flag kernel_selector=1.9 --reason "p95 tail regression"`
deploy-bot: deploybot:action: rewind_job started id=rewind-1779998888-1
samir: thanks — watching metrics. paging @oncall-ml for kernel selector context in case we need a hotpatch.
oncall-ml: on it, joining. quick note: the new kernel has improved average throughput but is more sensitive to small kv-cache TTL changes. good candidate for revert.
lia: status update draft (short): "We observed increased p95 latency in eu-west after a kernel selector change in 2.7.0. We're performing a staged rollback of the kernel flag to reduce tail latency. We'll update after each stage." ready to post when we move to 30%.
ops-oncall: step 1 stable after 5m — p95 down from 420ms -> 230ms, errors unchanged.
samir: ok proceed to 30%.
ops-oncall: executing step 2: `infractl rewind --region eu-west --slice 30 --flag kernel_selector=1.9`
deploy-bot: deploybot:action: rewind_job started id=rewind-1779998888-2
maya: running eval now
julian: eval: canary_smoke_v2: latency_ok=true, quality_regressions=false
ops-oncall: step 2 stable after 4m. p95 ~ 210ms.
ops-oncall: proceeding to 100% now.
deploy-bot: deploybot:action: rewind_job started id=rewind-1779998888-3
samir: good job. publishing status: "Staged rollback completed; kernel flag reset in eu-west. Monitoring for downstream impact. Postmortem to follow." posting to #incidents and release channels.
lia: create follow-up checklist: \n- create ticket for kernel selector decision and rollback rationale\n- verify dedicated/different regions to ensure no silent regressions\n- update model onboarding checklist to include kv-cache TTL compatibility test
maya: will draft release note amendment: short line in 2.7.0 notes about kernel selector fallback and a note to devs about kv-cache TTL.
samir: closing thread when postmortem ticket created.
ops-oncall: postmortem ticket created: INF-2026-444. marking thread resolved.
deploy-bot: deploybot:signal: rewind_job completed id=rewind-1779998888-3 status=success"
